title: Semilinear functors and comparison equations under raw scalar localization
statement:
Let $R,S$ be commutative rings, $t\in R$, $u\in S$, and $\phi:R\to S$ a unital ring homomorphism such that the image of $\phi(t)$ is invertible in $S[1/u]$. Let $\mathcal C$ be an $R$-linear category and $\mathcal D$ an $S$-linear category [def-weil-linear-category], and use their raw scalar localizations and localization functors $Q_R,Q_S$ of [def-weil-linear-scalar-localization]. Call an additive functor $F:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ $\phi$-semilinear when $F(rf)=\phi(r)F(f)$ for every scalar $r$ and morphism $f$.

Every such $F$ has a unique additive extension $\overline F:\mathcal C[1/t]\to\mathcal D[1/u]$, with the same object map, agreeing with $Q_SF$ on integral arrows and semilinear for the induced map $R[1/t]\to S[1/u]$. On fractions it is
$$\overline F(f/t^n)=\phi(t)^{-n}Q_S(F(f)).$$
For two such functors $F,G$ every natural transformation $\eta:F\Rightarrow G$ extends uniquely with components $Q_S(\eta_K)$. Natural isomorphisms extend to natural isomorphisms. These extensions preserve identity transformations, vertical composition and whiskering by composable semilinear functors (with compatible coefficient homomorphisms and inverted elements); consequently every well-typed equation of such composites remains true. In particular, unit, associator, shift and comparison-square equations on integral functors remain equations after scalar localization.

If the categories carry linear triangulated structures [def-weil-triangulated-category], their localizations have the induced shifts and distinguished triangles isomorphic to localized integral distinguished triangles as in [lem-weil-linear-scalar-localization-triangulated], and $F$ is exact with a specified linear shift comparison, then $\overline F$ is exact with the localized shift comparison. The same assertion applies to exact natural comparison isomorphisms.

source.place: Proof, finite-extension sentence: scalar transport between different valuation rings; generic semilinear localization lemma extracted from old Step 3

proof.text: Put $A=R[1/t]$, $B=S[1/u]$, and let $\lambda:S\to B$ be the localization map. Write $c=\lambda(\phi(t))$, which is a unit by hypothesis. Define $\bar\phi:A\to B$ by $\bar\phi(r/t^n)=\lambda(\phi(r))c^{-n}$. The fraction criterion of [def-weil-ring-localization-away] proves well-definedness: if $t^k(t^m r-t^n s)=0$, applying $\lambda\phi$ gives $c^k(c^m\lambda\phi(r)-c^n\lambda\phi(s))=0$; multiplication by $c^{-k-m-n}$ gives equality of the proposed images. The fraction addition and multiplication formulas show directly that $\bar\phi$ preserves addition, multiplication and $1$. Any extending ring map has to send $t^{-1}$ to $c^{-1}$, so this map is unique.

source.place: Tag 00CO, definition-localization and its fraction relation; elementary verification of the induced coefficient map

proof.text: For objects $K,L$ use the scalar-first tensor Hom modules in [def-weil-linear-scalar-localization]. Define the pairing $(a,f)\mapsto\bar\phi(a)\otimes F(f)$. It is additive in each argument. For $r\in R$, the coefficient-map equation on integral scalars and semilinearity of $F$ give $\bar\phi(ra)\otimes F(f)=\bar\phi(a)\otimes F(rf)$ by the tensor balancing relation over $S$. The balanced additive universal property, Mathlib TensorProduct.liftAddHom, produces an additive Hom map with this pure-tensor formula. Tensor induction proves that the formula determines the map uniquely: it fixes zero, pure tensors and sums.

source.place: Tags 07JZ and 07K0, definition-localization-module and lemma-universal-property-localization-module; Tag 00DK, lemma-tensor-localization

proof.text: The Hom maps of Step 2 are $\bar\phi$-semilinear: on pure tensors $(aa\prime)\otimes f$, the equality is exactly multiplicativity of $\bar\phi$, and tensor induction extends it to sums. Integral arrows have coefficient $1$, so their images agree with $Q_SF$. The coefficient map sends the inverse of $t$ to the inverse of its unit image, giving the stated fraction formula. For uniqueness, $a\otimes f=a(1\otimes f)$ forces every candidate image by semilinearity and integral agreement. Transport its prescribed object equalities, then apply tensor induction and functor extensionality.

source.place: Tags 07JZ and 00CO, fraction scalar-action formulas; elementary semilinearity and uniqueness calculation

proof.text:
Composition in the raw localized categories is bilinear and on pure tensors has the formula in [def-weil-linear-scalar-localization]. Thus for $f:K\to L$ and $g:L\to P$,
$$\overline F((g/t^m)\circ(f/t^n))=c^{-m-n}Q_S(F(gf))=(c^{-m}Q_S(F(g)))\circ(c^{-n}Q_S(F(f))).$$
Here the middle equality uses only the functor laws of $F$ and $Q_S$ and bilinearity in the target. Also $\overline F(1_K)=Q_S(F(1_K))=1_{FK}$. These equations give the functor laws, and Step 2 gives additivity on every Hom group. The extension therefore exists with every property asserted in the first clause.

source.place: Finite-extension sentence: elementary functor-law calculation for semilinear scalar transport

proof.text:
For $\eta:F\Rightarrow G$ define $\bar\eta_K=Q_S(\eta_K)$. For a fraction $f/t^n:K\to L$, integral naturality and the bilinearity of composition in [def-weil-linear-category] give
$$\overline G(f/t^n)\bar\eta_K=c^{-n}Q_S(G(f)\eta_K)=c^{-n}Q_S(\eta_LF(f))=\bar\eta_L\overline F(f/t^n).$$
Thus these components are natural on all localized arrows. Objects are unchanged, so the requirement on components determines the transformation uniquely. If $\eta$ is invertible, localize its inverse: $Q_S(\eta_K^{-1})Q_S(\eta_K)=1$ and $Q_S(\eta_K)Q_S(\eta_K^{-1})=1$ by the functor laws of [def-weil-linear-scalar-localization]. These are the inverse equations for $\bar\eta$.

source.place: Finite-extension sentence: naturality on fractions and the two inverse equations

proof.text: For composable semilinear functors $F$ and $H$, the induced coefficient map for the second functor sends the unit image of $t$ to a unit, verifying the composite inversion hypothesis. Applying the two semilinearity equations in succession gives semilinearity of $HF$. The coefficient maps agree on $R$ and hence on $R[1/t]$ by Step 1. Both extended composite functors send $a\otimes f$ to $\bar\psi(\bar\phi(a))\otimes H(F(f))$. Tensor induction proves equality of their arrow maps, and the object maps are definitionally equal. For identity and linear endofunctors the same argument identifies the extension with the identity and the existing tensor map.

source.place: Finite-extension sentence: composition of the explicit semilinear extensions; uses Steps 1–4

proof.text:
For composable transformations $\eta:F\Rightarrow G$, $\theta:G\Rightarrow J$, the component identities
$$Q_S(1_{FK})=1_{FK},\qquad Q_S(\theta_K\eta_K)=Q_S(\theta_K)Q_S(\eta_K)$$
show preservation of identities and vertical composition, by the functor laws of [def-weil-linear-scalar-localization]. Right whiskering with $H$ from Step 6 has component $\bar H(Q_S\eta_K)=Q_T(H\eta_K)$, because $\bar H$ agrees with $Q_T H$ on integral arrows. Left whiskering with a compatible preceding semilinear functor $P$ has component $Q_S(\eta_{PK})$, since the object map is unchanged. These are exactly the components of the localized integral whiskerings, with the endpoints identified in Step 6. By induction on a finite composite of these operations, its localized component is the localization of its integral component. Applying $Q$ to an integral equality then gives equality of the two localized components at every object. Hence the transformations are equal. This proves the claim about all well-typed unit, associator and comparison-square equations; the shift equations are included by taking the linear shifts as additional functors.

source.place: Finite-extension sentence: componentwise vertical-composition and whiskering calculation, then induction on composites

proof.text: Use the tensor Hom equivalence of the existing rationalization to compare the raw scalar localization with the categorical rationalization. This comparison is fully faithful and essentially surjective, so Q_R is a localization functor. Linearity of the shift by one implies linearity of every integer shift by induction and the shift equivalence. Apply Mathlib Functor.commShiftOfLocalization to Q_R, the composite F followed by Q_S, and the integral equality extension_spec. This supplies coherent comparisons for every integer shift. Its component formula is the image of the inverse comparison for Q_R, followed by the integral F comparison and the Q_S comparison. At one, the hypotheses hQC and hQD identify the outer comparisons with identity arrows; the lifting equality has identity components, giving precisely Q_S of the specified F comparison. The target image-triangle description makes Q_S exact. The lifting comparison commutes with shifts, hence Q_R followed by the extension is exact. Every distinguished source-localized triangle is isomorphic to Q_R of an integral distinguished triangle by hdistC. Apply the extension to this isomorphism and use the comparison for mapTriangle of a composite; closure under isomorphisms proves exactness of the extension.

source.place: Tag 05R6, proposition-construct-localization, distinguished triangles are those isomorphic to images of integral ones; exactness from that description

proof.text:
Finally take an exact natural comparison $\eta:(F,\sigma^F)\Rightarrow(G,\sigma^G)$. By [pur9-def-exact-transformation] its defining additional equation is
$$\sigma^G_K\eta_{K[1]}=\eta_K[1]\sigma^F_K.$$
Apply $Q_S$ to this equation. It preserves compositions and commutes with the induced shift by [def-weil-linear-scalar-localization], giving
$$\bar\sigma^G_K\bar\eta_{K[1]}=\bar\eta_K[1]\bar\sigma^F_K.$$
This is exactly the condition that $\bar\eta$ be a morphism of the exact functors of Step 8. If the comparison is invertible, Step 5 gives its localized inverse as well. The same componentwise argument applies to any of the shift compatibility equations among the comparisons of Step 7.

source.place: Defining equation of a morphism of exact functors, localized componentwise

proof_origin.place: Finite-extension sentence, realized by balanced tensor Hom maps, tensor induction, and coherent shift descent via categorical localization; exactness follows from the localized distinguished-triangle descriptions (Stacks 05R6).

Step 9 localizes the shift square.
